items: A rock face len long and h tall (3-60 m), running d back to a flat ledge on top. rug is how rugged the face is in metres either way, seed picks another rock; ledge is the thickness of the grass strip on top (0 = bare rock). A cliff is GROUND: the whole top, face band included, carries whatever you put on it, so draw the plateau first and run the cliff along its edge.

A tilted plateau with a rock face: h tall at the front (3-80 m), sloping down to the ground d back, with a grass strip ledge metres wide along the top edge. Its sloping top is GROUND — things placed on it land on it.
A tall rock column with a flat top — r is the mean radius (0.5-30 m), h the full height (3-80 m). Stand it in water. Its top disc is GROUND.
One rock sitting on the ground, 2r across. A real boulder is 0.3 to 4 m ACROSS (r 0.15 to 2); bigger is an outcrop, use a sea stack. seed gives a different lump of the same size.

count boulders scattered over w x d in a single record — stony ground, a moraine, an outcrop field. size is the LARGEST boulder's DIAMETER (0.3-4 m); the rest run from 0.4 to 1.0 of it and 30 % are the lighter stone. gx and gz are the ground slope (rise per metre) along the record's local x and z: each rock's base drops onto that plane while the rock stays upright.
A rubble slope len long: h tall at the -Z edge (0.5-40 m), falling to nothing w across. Put it at the foot of a cliff. Its wedge surface is GROUND.
